routes.description: Establish that Christian theism provides a rationally coherent account of nature, human reason, objective value, suffering, and human purpose, then connect that general theistic account to the biblical God through the historical claims concerning Jesus.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the cumulative scientific, philosophical, moral, existential, and historical considerations make belief in the biblical God rational while adequately addressing naturalistic alternatives, the evidential burden for miracles, and the challenge from undeserved suffering.

motionBridge.description: Show that the cumulative case supports rational belief specifically in the biblical God, rather than merely an unspecified creator.

centralBridges.description: Show that cosmic order, intelligibility, and reliable rational minds are coherently explained by an ultimate rational creator.
Show that divine creation grounds objective morality, equal human worth, and an ultimate purpose not supplied by unguided processes alone.
Supply sufficient historical grounds for treating Jesus, the resurrection, and the New Testament witness as evidence identifying the creator with the biblical God.
Reconcile the biblical God's goodness and power with suffering through divine participation, compensation, justice, and enduring hope.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why stable natural laws do not logically exclude exceptional divine agency and why miracle claims remain open to historical assessment.
Distinguish evidence-responsive Christian commitment from unsupported belief and state the evidential role assigned to Gospel testimony.

routes.description: Establish that naturalistic explanations and secular accounts of reason, morality, meaning, and hope remove the need for a divine hypothesis, while suffering and weaknesses in the historical case count against belief in the biblical God.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalistic and secular alternatives explain the relevant phenomena without God and if the proposed scientific, philosophical, moral, and historical grounds do not meet the burden required for rational belief in an omnipotent, omniscient, wholly good biblical deity.

motionBridge.description: Show that the available considerations do not justify belief specifically in the biblical God under present standards of rational inquiry.

centralBridges.description: Show that cosmology, evolution, and natural processes can account for origins and apparent design without adding a divine explanatory entity.
Show that evolved rational capacities can track truth and support objective moral reasons without requiring a divine foundation.
Show that extensive undeserved human and nonhuman suffering is evidentially difficult to reconcile with the biblical God's asserted attributes.
Show that the evidence for resurrection, scriptural reliability, and Jesus's divine authority is insufficient for the extraordinary historical conclusions asserted.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Account for religious commitment through cultural transmission and require independent evidence capable of overcoming that contingency.
Show that finite purposes, practical efforts against suffering, and meaningful hope remain available without immortality or externally assigned purpose.

sections.title: Science, Origins, Design, and Rational Mind
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether cosmic intelligibility, apparent design, biological complexity, and reliable cognition favor an ultimate rational creator or are adequately explained by cosmology, evolution, and naturalistic accounts of mind.

sections.title: Objective Morality, Human Worth, and Purpose
sections.rationale: This issue bears on whether objective moral reasons, equal human value, and ultimate purpose require creation in God's image or can arise through rational impartiality and self-directed secular purposes.

sections.title: Jesus, Resurrection, and Scriptural Reliability
sections.rationale: This issue supplies the necessary bridge from generic theism to the biblical God by testing the historical evidence for resurrection, the coherence of miracle claims, and the reliability and authority of New Testament testimony.

sections.title: Suffering, Hope, Compensation, and Justice
sections.rationale: This issue directly tests the compatibility of extensive undeserved suffering with the biblical God's goodness and power, alongside competing accounts of consolation, practical mitigation, afterlife compensation, and final justice.

sections.title: Faith, Cultural Contingency, and Explanatory Burden
sections.rationale: This issue examines whether invoking God improves explanation and whether Christian commitment is evidence-responsive despite concerns about unsupported faith, inherited religious affiliation, and the availability of an uncreated natural reality.
